sections.heading: 1. Assign four accountable seats before expanding to six
paragraphs: Structure Candidate #20 as four accountable people, not four departments. The first full-time seat is the owner-originator: they qualify commercial borrowers, control lender relationships, approve placement strategy, and own fee negotiations. The second full-time seat is the placement and operations lead: they maintain the lender matrix, inspect complete packages, track conditions, and reconcile closing evidence. Contractor one provides document assembly and borrower follow-up against a purchased deliverable; contractor two supplies specialist underwriting support and independent package review. Neither contractor promises credit approval, changes lender terms, or receives borrower funds. A HubSpot deal record identifies one accountable employee, while SharePoint stores versioned borrower evidence with access limited to the assigned file. Equipment, accounts-receivable, SBA, and bridge placements share this operating spine but retain separate document checklists and lender eligibility fields. Across the 29 mapped operator plays, this is a finance-intermediary model, not a balance-sheet lending business or a collection of 29 products. Two contractors remain two people even when their work spans several product lanes. Reject staffing plans that hide recurring processing labor inside unnamed vendors or assume the owner can originate continuously while checking every bank statement.

Buy contractor outputs with measurable acceptance criteria rather than rewarding submission volume. An illustrative document-package engagement pays $300 for an accepted assembly and $75 for a separately authorized material refresh; a specialist review pays $250 for a completed credit memorandum covering the agreed scope. These are procurement assumptions, not fee-market benchmarks or additions to canonical revenue. A package passes only when borrower identity, entity authority, requested amount, source documents, reconciled schedules, and lender-specific requirements match the assignment. Require acknowledgment within one business day, delivery within two business days after complete inputs, and correction of contractor-caused defects within one business day without a second fee. Pause the delivery clock for missing borrower evidence and record the dependency explicitly. The employee lead accepts every package and reviews all critical fields; weekly sampling tests the remaining checklist items. Do not convert independent deliverables into employee-style daily supervision merely by labeling workers contractors. Evaluate classification under applicable federal and state tests, including California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant and any applicable exception. If the actual relationship requires employment, change the staffing model rather than concealing the mismatch in a services agreement.

Expand to 3 FT + 3 C only after the existing pod demonstrates capacity pressure and positive collected contribution through at least two complete closing cohorts. Add a full-time relationship and renewal manager to remove routine borrower follow-up from the owner, then add one contractor for peak document intake and source-data reconciliation. The operations lead retains final package acceptance; the specialist contractor remains independent of the assembly they review. Track employee and contractor hours separately, because six named people do not imply six full-time equivalents. The canonical annual expense envelopes are $90,000 Conservative, $364,000 Base, and $550,000 Scaled: retained-fee revenue minus the specified owner profit. Those totals must contain actual payroll, contractor fees, systems, insurance, marketing, and other operating costs. The Conservative envelope is especially tight for two full-time seats; disclose owner compensation treatment and local wage requirements instead of assuming two market-rate salaries fit. Preserve the canonical $30,000 profit as the scenario target, while recording any actual budget shortfall separately. Before hiring, stress the thirteen-week cash schedule for a ninety-day closing delay and a contractually supportable clawback event. Capacity expansion follows cash resilience, not submitted loan principal.

callout.title: Buy clean credit packages, not performative activity
callout.body: Protect the four-person pod by making evidence reusable while keeping lender-specific judgments explicit.
items: Require the AR specialist to reconcile the aging total to the general ledger and identify dilution, offsets, and concentrated account debtors before lender matching.
Store equipment quotes, serial identifiers, useful-life assumptions, and lien-search dates as separate fields so a changed asset does not silently reuse stale underwriting.
For bridge placements, distinguish sponsor liquidity from projected refinance proceeds and record the specific maturity exit assumption reviewed by the lender.
For SBA work, maintain the current agent-services scope, compensation evidence, and applicable SBA Form 159 documentation rather than copying conventional brokerage fee language.

sections.heading: 2. Run a weekly cohort scorecard with explicit concentration limits
paragraphs: Run Monday's operator meeting from a frozen Friday extract, not a live dashboard that changes during discussion. Maintain one deal identifier across HubSpot, the document repository, and QuickBooks Online. The scorecard separates qualified mandates, complete packages, lender decisions, funded closings, earned retained fees, and collected fees. Define a qualified mandate as a borrower with verified business purpose, a documented financing request, a plausible repayment source, and authorization for the proposed brokerage work. A lender submission counts only when the lender receives an accepted package; sending another email does not create another opportunity. Measure package acceptance against all first deliveries, including rejected deliveries. Measure close rate by submission cohort and product lane after a stated observation window, reporting open cases separately instead of treating them as wins or losses. The operations lead owns data definitions, while the owner chooses one corrective action for each breached threshold. Contractor invoices reference accepted deliverable identifiers, preventing payment for duplicate packages. Every correction has an accountable person and a next review date. This turns weekly reporting into a control loop rather than a sales meeting dominated by the largest prospective principal amount.

Use the Base case to translate annual ambition into unit economics without changing the canonical scorecard. Forty funded placements at an average $14,000 retained fee produce $560,000 annual recognized revenue; $364,000 expenses leave $196,000 owner profit and a 35.0% margin. This is an illustrative fee mix, not a prediction that every equipment or SBA closing produces that fee. At a 40% mature-cohort funding rate, forty closings require one hundred complete submissions annually, approximately 1.9 per calendar week. A 50% qualified-mandate-to-submission rate would require two hundred qualified mandates, approximately 3.8 weekly. Display these denominators beside observed rates and report medians plus ninetieth-percentile cycle times; averages alone hide stalled bridge files and prolonged SBA conditions. Set initial internal service targets of at least 95% first-pass package acceptance and no unresolved critical evidence defects at submission. These are operating targets to calibrate against actual cohorts, not lender promises. Track fees per accepted package, review hours per closing, and collected contribution by product. A low-fee product can consume the same employee attention as a high-fee placement, so revenue growth without capacity economics can reduce owner profit.

Set a maximum 25% share for each economically connected borrower group and each lender group, measured separately against trailing-twelve-month retained-fee revenue. Consolidate affiliates; four lender brands sharing one credit platform do not automatically create four independent counterparties. Track referral-source concentration and expected pipeline fees with the same 25% operating limit, while keeping forecast exposure distinct from recognized revenue. At Base revenue, the annual ceiling is $140,000 per group; at Scaled revenue it is $250,000. For a new book, the first closing necessarily creates concentration above the limit. Label that startup condition nondiversified, do not describe the cap as achieved, and route growth toward independent borrowers, sources, and lenders. A breach stops additional discretionary exposure to the affected group while the owner addresses contracted obligations and develops alternatives. Never route an unsuitable borrower merely to improve a dashboard ratio. Maintain two credible placement alternatives for each active product lane, documenting geography, collateral, ticket size, and current appetite. Fair-lending controls also apply to routing: Regulation B covers certain referral participants for its antidiscrimination and discouragement provisions. Use documented credit criteria, not protected characteristics or unsupported geographic proxies.

sections.heading: 3. Build a transferable fee ledger, evidence chain and rights package
paragraphs: Make the retained-fee ledger explain every dollar without using loan principal as brokerage revenue. Each deal record holds signed fee terms, the service performance trigger, funding evidence, the retained amount, invoice date, cash receipt, referral obligations, and any contractual recovery period. Under the applicable accrual policy, recognize revenue when the brokerage's performance obligation is satisfied and the amount is supportable, not when a borrower accepts a preliminary term sheet. Evaluate variable consideration and reversal exposure under the chosen accounting framework; a cash reserve is not itself an accounting expense or a substitute for that analysis. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation for third-party amounts rather than mechanically netting every payment. The canonical operating scorecard remains retained origination or referral fees only, with a reconciliation to the general ledger if presentation differs. Separate expected clawback adjustments from credit-loss allowances on already earned receivables. QuickBooks Online can carry the accounting entries while a controlled deal subledger carries lender and cohort detail. Reconcile monthly opening receivables plus earned fees minus receipts, credits, and write-offs to closing receivables. Never let a dashboard silently overwrite previously reported cohorts after a failed closing.

Prepare transferability while the book is small. Every contractor agreement should identify pre-existing tools, assign specified newly created copyrightable deliverables through a signed writing, and grant necessary rights to embedded background materials. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a copyright ownership transfer generally requires a writing signed by the owner or their authorized agent. Do not rely on a work-made-for-hire label for every independent contractor spreadsheet or memorandum. Store the executed assignment beside the deliverable inventory and retain source versions of checklists, lender-matrix structures, training materials, and automations. An IP assignment does not transfer ownership of borrower records, override confidentiality terms, or authorize unrestricted data sale. Inventory lender agreements for assignment restrictions, change-of-control provisions, termination rights, and commission survival. Borrower engagements need their own transfer and information-sharing analysis. Maintain company-controlled accounts, multifactor authentication, role-based access, and a documented contractor offboarding routine. Where the business is a covered institution, implement the FTC Safeguards Rule under 16 CFR Part 314, including applicable service-provider oversight. Give prospective buyers aggregated cohort evidence first, then controlled file access only when confidentiality and data-sharing requirements support it.

Create a monthly close packet that a buyer can reproduce without interviewing the founder. Include the trial balance, deal-level revenue bridge, bank reconciliation, open commission aging, clawback schedule, contractor acceptance register, and concentration report. Reconcile Conservative revenue of $120,000 to $90,000 expenses and $30,000 profit; Base revenue of $560,000 to $364,000 expenses and $196,000 profit; and Scaled revenue of $1,000,000 to $550,000 expenses and $450,000 profit. Keep these scenarios distinct from actual results and identify the period covered by every actual statement. Track submission cohorts for operational conversion and funding cohorts for fee realization and subsequent recoveries. A lender switch should preserve the original deal identifier and decision history. Maintain a jurisdiction-and-product register covering the activity performed, licensing or exemption basis, required fee disclosures, and responsible employee. California Financing Law section 22100 requires licensing for covered finance-lender or broker activity unless an exemption applies; commercial purpose alone does not settle the analysis. SBA agent compensation has separate requirements under 13 CFR Part 103. Keep securities introductions outside the ordinary debt-placement workflow pending a separate broker-dealer registration analysis under 15 U.S.C. section 78o.

sections.heading: 4. Price transferable earnings, then compare an exit with continued ownership
paragraphs: A buyer pays for repeatable earnings they can operate, not for funded principal or projected renewals. Begin with the canonical owner-profit figures, then construct a separate earnings bridge for the contemplated buyer. Owner net profit, seller discretionary earnings, and EBITDA are different measures; identify owner wages, benefits, financing costs, taxes, and necessary replacement labor before choosing a multiple. For an owner-operator acquisition, an illustrative negotiation sensitivity of 2.0 to 3.0 times normalized discretionary earnings can frame a small, concentrated book. A genuinely manager-run, diversified operation might be tested at 3.0 to 4.5 times normalized EBITDA. These are underwriting assumptions, not observed transaction comparables or an automatic premium attached to finance brokerage. Thin retained-fee history, weak assignment rights, customer dependence, or a departing founder can push a transaction below those ranges or into an asset-only structure. Ask bidders to state the earnings definition, included working capital, assumed liabilities, and consideration form. A larger headline multiple with contingent payments may produce less certain value than a smaller cash offer. Candidate #20's score of 89/100 measures the operating opportunity across 29 mapped plays; it is not a valuation formula.

Model the Base transfer with explicit replacement-cost assumptions. If its $196,000 owner profit includes no separate owner wage expense, and a buyer must spend $100,000 annually to replace the owner's necessary work, transferable earnings before other adjustments fall to $96,000. At an illustrative 3.0 times that earnings measure, indicated enterprise value is $288,000. If equivalent replacement labor is already fully expensed, do not subtract it again. For the Scaled case, the same additional $100,000 assumption reduces $450,000 owner profit to $350,000; a 3.0 to 4.5 times sensitivity then indicates $1,050,000 to $1,575,000 enterprise value before debt, cash, working-capital, transaction-cost, and other adjustments. The Conservative $30,000 profit cannot absorb that replacement assumption, so a manager-run earnings valuation would be inappropriate without operating changes. None of these bridges revises canonical revenue or profit. They test transfer economics under a stated buyer structure. As a simple timing sensitivity, two years of unchanged Base owner profit totals $392,000 before personal taxes and reinvestment, but requires continued work and exposes the owner to closing and recovery risk. Compare risk-adjusted cash flows and workload rather than equating that sum with an immediately payable sale price.

Earn a stronger valuation by removing specific buyer objections before entering a process. Demonstrate twelve months of reproducible monthly closes, a second employee relationship on active accounts, documented renewal execution, and concentration within the 25% limits. Show that another employee can complete a placement using the lender matrix without the founder supplying undocumented criteria. Do not count uncommitted renewals as contracted recurring revenue; present historical renewal cohorts, fee realization, and borrower attrition instead. For contingent consideration, define the transferred customer cohort, collection window, retained-fee calculation, permitted deductions, and treatment of lender-imposed clawbacks. An earnout based on collected retained fees can be easier to audit than one based on buyer-controlled overhead, but still needs servicing obligations, reporting access, and dispute mechanics. Separate enterprise value from proceeds paid at closing and proceeds that depend on future performance. If bids do not compensate for giving up a durable cash stream, retain the business and apply the same transferability controls internally. The cash-cow version still needs contractor quality checks, lender redundancy, security maintenance, and replacement capacity. A brokerage becomes durable when its evidence and relationships survive a person's absence, not when its owner stops looking at the scorecard.

chapters.question_prompt: What is the exact Day-1-to-Day-30 execution schedule for launching specialty finance brokerage, and what quantitative thresholds govern Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions at Day 30/60/90?
chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A Four-Person Equipment, Receivables, SBA and Bridge Placement Sprint Using Lender Matrices, Fee Controls and Measured Stop Rules
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #20, Specialty Finance Brokerage, ranks #06 among the series' 29 mapped plays with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 89/100. Launch one commercial financing lane with two full-time operators and two contractors, not four simultaneous product desks. The first month must produce a documented lender matrix, permissioned borrower files, written compensation terms and measurable lender engagement within an $8,000 cash ceiling. Day 30/60/90 decisions distinguish broken distribution from ordinary closing latency: first revenue commonly takes three to nine months. Canonical annual owner profits are $30,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base and $450,000 Scaled. These are retained-fee business outcomes, never financed principal. Expand only after independent lender coverage, qualified-file conversion and executable fee economics survive explicit thresholds.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1-7: Narrow the Lane, Assign the Pod and Cap Cash Exposure
paragraphs: Start Candidate #20 as one narrowly specified placement desk within the series' 29 mapped operator plays. Select equipment acquisition financing for established businesses, receivables financing for business invoices, SBA placement, or a defined commercial bridge niche; do not combine their application requirements into one universal intake. Score the initial lane against existing borrower access, contractor expertise, lender availability and licensing cost. An equipment desk needs asset descriptions, vendor invoices, useful life and lien information; an AR desk needs aging, dilution, debtor concentration and assignability analysis. An SBA desk adds program eligibility and compensation documentation; a bridge desk adds collateral valuation, exit evidence and maturity risk. Record one exclusion list, including consumer-purpose requests and securities placements outside the authorized operating scope. The founder owns borrower qualification and lender relationships. The second full-time operator owns packaging, document custody and the pipeline ledger. One contractor provides capped underwriting support; the other covers scoped licensing, agreements and security implementation through appropriately qualified specialists. Contractor status does not remove access controls or supervisory responsibility. Limit active packaging to six files until measured handling time supports more, and assign every file exactly one accountable internal owner.

Days one through three establish authority before outreach creates obligations. Build a jurisdiction worksheet covering the brokerage location, borrower location, collateral location, product, compensation source and relevant exemptions. California Financial Code section 22100, for example, establishes licensing requirements for finance lenders and brokers subject to applicable exceptions; a commercial borrower alone does not establish an exemption. Have qualified counsel resolve the actual transaction model rather than copying another broker's website disclosures. For SBA transactions, map 13 CFR 103.5 and current SBA Form 159 instructions to each compensated service, payer and reporting responsibility. Identify who makes credit decisions and who communicates adverse action. Regulation B includes referral participants within its creditor definition for specified nondiscrimination provisions, so a referral label does not eliminate every fair-lending duty. Prepare an engagement letter identifying services, fee trigger, payer, refund provisions, lender independence and information sharing. Do not promise approval, rate, funding date or government endorsement. Where securities placement is implicated, stop that workflow and assess Exchange Act registration requirements separately. Finish the week with written permission boundaries: what the desk may solicit, package, transmit and invoice, and which unresolved cases it must decline or refer elsewhere.

Use an illustrative $40,000 opening cash balance and an $8,000 first-month disbursement ceiling, inside the canonical $20,000-$100,000 startup range and $4,000-$18,000 monthly operating range. Allocate $2,400 to scoped legal and licensing work, $1,600 to underwriting support, $900 to secure software and insurance deposits, $1,100 to targeted acquisition, and $2,000 to essential administration and agreed cash draws. These are planning allocations, not vendor quotations; an unaffordable license or insurance requirement changes the lane before money is committed. Two full-time operators describes working capacity, not a claim that this ceiling funds two market salaries. Document deferred founder compensation and its economic cost separately. Cap cumulative disbursements at $16,000 on day sixty and $24,000 on day ninety, with outstanding noncancelable commitments deducted when measuring available cash. The resulting $16,000 balance at day ninety funds only two additional months at the ceiling. A nine-month no-revenue plan needs $72,000 of operating cash plus a $10,000 reserve, or a lower documented burn. A $20,000 capitalization cannot support this schedule unchanged. Require a credible runway reduction or committed capital before the business reaches that constraint; projected commissions do not count as available cash.

callout.body: Each check requires retained evidence and a named internal owner, not a verbal assurance.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8-14: Build a Financeable Funnel Instead of a Lead Count
paragraphs: Build the lender matrix before purchasing volume. Each lender row records product, geography, minimum and maximum facility size, borrower tenure, financial thresholds, collateral policy, guaranty expectations, excluded industries, document requirements, turnaround targets, fee terms and recourse provisions. Separate lenders sharing the same ultimate credit committee; three brand names using one funding source represent one independent outlet for concentration measurement. Request a current written appetite confirmation and refresh it every thirty days during the sprint. A lender counts as usable only when its identified contact confirms the lane, agrees to receive permissioned files and supplies written broker compensation terms. Distinguish eligibility rules from underwriting discretion: a published minimum credit score does not mean every applicant above it qualifies. For equipment, ask about used assets, private sellers, soft costs and titled collateral. For receivables, ask about cross-aging, government debtors, dilution reserves and notification requirements. For SBA, ask which program and current eligibility interpretation the lender actually supports. For bridge transactions, require explicit lien-position, valuation and exit requirements. Use matching automation to surface candidate lenders and missing documents, never to represent that a lender has approved a borrower. Save dated rule versions so rejected matches can be diagnosed against the criteria used.

Define a qualified conversation as an interaction with an authorized business representative who confirms financing purpose, approximate amount, timing, operating history and permission for a specific next step. An email open or downloaded checklist does not qualify. A complete application is a unique borrower request containing the selected lane's mandatory documents, a recorded permission scope and a reconciled use of proceeds. A lender-accepted review means a named lender acknowledges that the file is sufficiently complete to enter underwriting; it is neither an automated receipt nor a credit approval. Count each borrower once for conversion even when two lenders review the same file. Target thirty qualified conversations and ten complete applications cumulatively by day thirty. During week two, approach fifteen equipment vendors, accountants, fractional CFOs or other lane-specific introducers individually, seeking actual transaction referrals rather than purchased lists. Document any introducer compensation before accepting referrals and check its permissibility for the product and jurisdiction. Maintain lead-source attribution through closing, payment and any later reversal. Track the reason each prospect declines, because poor timing, unfinanceable collateral and disagreement over broker fees require different fixes. Keep borrower demographic information out of marketing prioritization and review referral patterns for prohibited discriminatory steering.

Apply data minimization to the document request, not merely to the software subscription. Collect business tax returns, bank statements, receivables schedules and guarantor information only when the selected financing path needs them. Use a borrower-specific SharePoint folder with restricted sharing, multifactor authentication and an access register; a CRM should hold status and document links rather than duplicate sensitive attachments. Determine whether the operation is a financial institution covered by the FTC Safeguards Rule, 16 CFR Part 314, using its actual activities and the rule's scope. Where applicable, implement the required information-security program and assess service providers; specific exceptions do not justify abandoning baseline safeguards. Preserve permission evidence, submission versions and deletion schedules, while reconciling retention with applicable credit-record requirements. Do not transmit a full borrower package to every lender in the matrix. First perform a limited-data appetite check, then share the authorized package with selected recipients. Record who received which version and why. At the end of each day, reconcile incomplete files, expiring permissions and contractor access. The operations lead should be able to answer a borrower's sharing question from the ledger without searching personal inboxes or relying on the founder's memory.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15-21: Submit Clean Files and Underwrite the Broker's Own Economics
paragraphs: Week three tests whether the desk can convert documents into genuine credit attention without exhausting its four-person pod. Send each selected lender a concise transaction memo covering borrower operations, requested facility, use of proceeds, repayment source, collateral, existing obligations and exceptions. Attach a document index and identify unresolved issues plainly. For equipment, reconcile invoice amount, down payment and requested advance; for receivables, reconcile eligible balances after aging exclusions and concentration limits. For secured bridge requests, identify prior liens and ask the lender or closing professional to resolve priority under applicable state UCC Article 9 provisions or real-property law. Do not treat a preliminary lien search as a completed title or priority opinion. For SBA, align service descriptions and compensation records with the applicable program requirements. Require acknowledgment from a named lender contact and log the first substantive underwriting request. Schedule two fixed lender follow-up blocks per week instead of interrupting file production continuously. If a lender misses its stated response target, escalate once and use another authorized outlet. Preserve the decline reason as a specific matrix update; do not repeatedly resubmit the same defective package under a different filename.

Model brokerage economics on retained fees only. An illustrative $500,000 funded facility with a contractual two-percent broker fee produces $10,000 of gross broker compensation, not $500,000 of revenue. If an enforceable arrangement allocates $2,000 to an outside referral party, use $8,000 as the retained-fee planning basis. Have the accountant determine the appropriate gross or net financial-statement presentation for the actual contracts, and reconcile that presentation back to the scorecard basis. At $8,000 retained per funding, fifteen annual fundings produce the Conservative $120,000 revenue case, seventy produce the Base $560,000 case, and 125 produce the Scaled $1,000,000 case. Applying the canonical margins yields exactly $30,000, $196,000 and $450,000 annual owner net profit. Corresponding total annual cost envelopes are $90,000, $364,000 and $550,000. Those envelopes include the modeled business's full costs; the monthly operating range is not a substitute for annual variable-cost and staffing analysis. Conservative and Base retain two full-time operators plus two contractors. Scaled uses three plus three, so its throughput cannot be assigned casually to the launch pod. These funding counts illustrate one fee size, not a forecast that overrides actual lender agreements or the three-to-nine-month first-deal window.

Maintain separate ledgers for retained-fee opportunity, earned revenue, receivables and collected cash. A signed term sheet contributes to a scenario forecast but creates no automatic recognized revenue. Determine the earning event and accounting treatment from the contract and applicable accounting policy; reconcile lender remittances against invoices when money arrives. For operating decisions, calculate expected contribution per accepted review as documented funding probability multiplied by retained fee, less expected reversals and all incremental acquisition, packaging and closing costs. With a provisional twenty-percent funding probability, $8,000 retained fee, $160 probability-weighted reversal allowance and $900 incremental cost, expected contribution is $540. At ten-percent funding probability, holding those other assumptions constant, it becomes negative $260. Neither probability is an observed conversion rate without a suitable funded cohort; use the downside result to limit exposure. Track actual cash-funded reversal reserves separately from this expected-loss calculation. Read clawback triggers for early payoff, cancellation, fraud and lender payment errors before spending commission receipts. Record contractor hours by file and source so bad packaging economics cannot hide inside general overhead. By day twenty-one, the founder should know which file types deserve more attention, which require a pricing repair and which consume effort without a credible path to retained compensation.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22-30 and Beyond: Execute Quantitative Kill, Fix or Scale Decisions
paragraphs: Day twenty-two is the source audit: rank introducers by complete applications and documented handling hours, not contact volume. Day twenty-three is the lender audit: confirm independent decision outlets and investigate every overdue acknowledgment. Day twenty-four is the borrower audit: resolve missing items and close records without an agreed next action. Day twenty-five is the fee audit: reconcile written compensation, outside allocations and reversal provisions for every live placement. Day twenty-six is the cash audit: compare disbursements and commitments with the $8,000 ceiling and rebuild the no-revenue runway. Day twenty-seven is the security exercise: revoke a test contractor account, inspect sharing logs and recover a test document. Day twenty-eight is the capacity exercise: measure handling hours and identify which checklist or lender-matching improvement would remove the largest recurring delay. Day twenty-nine produces the decision packet with frozen denominators, dated lender evidence and downside economics. Day thirty assigns Kill, Fix or Scale to the lane and to each acquisition source. Keep renewal tracking active even before first funding by recording existing facility maturities and borrower-requested follow-up dates. Never let a renewal reminder imply permission to distribute a fresh application. The founder signs the decision; the operations lead preserves its supporting snapshot.

Use cumulative complete-file targets of ten, twenty and thirty at days thirty, sixty and ninety, alongside cumulative qualified-conversation targets of thirty, sixty and ninety. Conversion uses matured complete applications: files completed at least ten business days before the checkpoint. Divide unique borrowers accepted into lender review by that denominator; younger files remain visible but cannot depress or inflate this ratio. Require at least five matured files at day thirty and ten at subsequent checkpoints before labeling conversion Scale or applying its percentage-based Kill rule. Smaller samples are Fix. For distribution, zero complete files after thirty qualified conversations supports killing that source even without a matured cohort. Lender concentration uses the largest independent lender's accepted-review count divided by all lender-specific accepted reviews; it is deliberately different from borrower conversion. The matrix's thresholds are management test rules, not industry benchmarks. Evaluate every row, apply Kill if any applicable Kill condition is met, and allow Scale only when all Scale conditions hold. Everything else is Fix with an owner, a single changed variable and a fourteen-day retest. Legal authority failures, unauthorized disclosure, unreliable borrower evidence or inability to pay committed obligations override commercial results and stop the affected activity immediately.

Scale means a controlled increase in tested activity, not hiring toward the six-person scenario because a dashboard turns green. At day thirty, permit at most ten-percent additional weekly qualified outreach while keeping the $8,000 monthly ceiling and six-file packaging limit. At days sixty and ninety, permit at most twenty-percent additional outreach per checkpoint, provided measured capacity absorbs it and every matrix condition remains satisfied. Retained-fee terms must support nonnegative downside contribution before expansion; a favorable central estimate alone earns Fix. Recalculate runway after the proposed increase, excluding speculative collections and deducting commitments. Zero funded deals at day ninety is compatible with the canonical three-to-nine-month first-deal interval if real underwriting progress exists. Conversely, an early closing does not repair a one-lender dependency or an exhausted cash balance. Kill normally means retiring the failed lane, source or lender relationship, preserving required records and completing existing contractual duties. A business-wide pause applies when the underlying authority, security or liquidity failure affects every lane. Do not move into a replacement niche without repeating its authority and lender-fit checks. Release additional staffing only after collected retained fees and measured workload support it; reconcile the resulting annual model to the canonical revenue, margin and team cases rather than annualizing a single successful month.

By Day 7, assign the two full-time operators and two contractors, establish a six-file packaging limit and approve the $8,000 first-month cash ceiling.
